summary: After an X (Twitter) quarrel between Conor McGregor and Canelo Alvarez, the article speculates about a crossover boxing match and its financial impact. It argues the bout could add $55-60 million to Canelo's $180 million net worth, moving him closer to Floyd Mayweather's $450 million. It supports this with both fighters' past pay-per-view numbers and the shared history of each with Mayweather.
one_line: A hypothetical Canelo Alvarez vs. Conor McGregor boxing match, sparked by an X feud, could boost Canelo's net worth toward Floyd Mayweather's.
key_facts: The Canelo Alvarez–Conor McGregor feud began on X (formerly Twitter) when McGregor praised Mayweather's 2013 performance against Canelo and boasted he landed more punches on Mayweather than Canelo did.
Canelo replied that he would need only one hand to make quick work of McGregor.
Canelo Alvarez became the first undisputed super-middleweight champion, holding the WBA Super, WBC and Ring Magazine titles since 2020 and the IBF and WBO titles since 2021.
Canelo's net worth is stated as $180 million in 2023, boosted by a $365 million deal with DAZN and Golden Boy Promotions.

Canelo's fight with Mayweather drew 2.2 million PPV buys; his 2017 bout with Julio César Chávez Jr. drew 1 million; the first Gennady Golovkin fight drew 1.3 million; the recent Jermell Charlo fight drew 700K.
McGregor's PPV numbers: 4.3 million for Mayweather, 1.6 million for the second Dustin Poirier fight, 2.4 million for Khabib Nurmagomedov, and 1.65 million for the second Nate Diaz fight.
Floyd Mayweather is described as the richest boxer in the world, with a net worth of $450 million, and is said to have made over a billion dollars across his career.
Canelo's biggest purse to date is $45 million, from his third fight with Golovkin.
The article estimates a McGregor fight could earn Canelo $55 to $60 million, lifting his net worth to about $240 million.
Revenue sources for such a fight would include pay-per-view sales, live gate, merchandise and promotional events.
McGregor made his boxing debut against Mayweather, losing the fight but earning a large payday.
Canelo's Jermell Charlo fight took place at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, with weigh-ins on September 29, 2023.
